Replay

Deterministic peer rollback

8 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Input and confirmation contractDeterminism and trustArchives and participant recoveryImplemented behavior and remaining M7 work

Use Runner(State, Input, Event, Seats) for a fixed-roster match whose peers replay the same deterministic simulation. The runner schedules steps and manages input delivery, prediction and rollback independently of the server-authoritative runner. Each participant owns its input stream and simulates the same complete match. No participant supplies authoritative state corrections to another.

Odin
model := p2p.Model(World, Input, Event, 2){
    step = step_world,
    input_valid = valid_input,
    state_valid = valid_world,
    hold = predict_missing_input,
}
error := p2p.init(&peer, initial_frame, model, roster, local_slot, transport)
error = p2p.pump(&peer, monotonic_ms)
result := p2p.advance(&peer, sampled_input)
// Consume device edges when result.captured. Consume the clock tick on success.
// Waiting preserves the already captured future input and stalls simulation.

The roster is ordered, fixed and supplied by an external admission/transport provider. Slot numbers are zero-based. Transport peer IDs determine input ownership; packets cannot name another slot. The native Godot example establishes two peers through an ENet listening/dialing pair. Listening chooses the transport topology, not a simulation authority. A larger roster requires full-mesh delivery through the transport abstraction. Native tests exercise two- and three-peer meshes.

Input and confirmation contract#

  • Session/epoch/content, ordered roster, schema, tick rate, delay, history, prediction limit and initial state hash are gated before play.
  • The first delay ticks after the initial checkpoint use known neutral input. advance captures one immutable local sample for head + delay + 1. A repeated call while stalled does not replace that sample. Result.captured identifies the capture boundary for short presses; it is separate from successful stepping.
  • Peers resend bounded windows starting at their oldest unacknowledged input. An ACK confirms receipt only; it does not confirm simulation or global settlement of gameplay. Inputs arriving out of order advance the contiguous receipt frontier only after all earlier samples are present.
  • Missing remote input is derived with hold(previous). A changed late input replays the complete affected suffix, refreshing guesses from actual received samples. replay.revise_inputs commits that suffix transactionally without incorrectly confirming still-guessed earlier ticks.
  • A tick is confirmed only when inputs from every participant are known. The prediction horizon limits how far simulation can run ahead. If a blackout exhausts that horizon, the runner returns Waiting and stops advancing instead of selecting one peer's world for resynchronization. Local input history is retained until peers acknowledge it.
  • A rolling checksum chains every confirmed canonical state and occurrence batch. Disagreement produces a Diverged phase and mismatch tick/peer/hash diagnostics. Conflicting values for an already received input fail the match. The runner does not silently pick a winner or merge states.

The wire uses canonical RPLY framing, fixed-size input windows and bounded decode storage. Input schemas are limited to 256 wire bytes; packet size is at most 8192 bytes. The pump receives at most 64 packets per call. Configuration allows 2–8 seats, 32–1024 history frames and a prediction+delay horizon below history capacity. Runtime owners contain allocations and must remain at stable addresses.

Determinism and trust#

The runner rejects float-bearing state/input/event schemas and platform-sized integer fields. This is a useful constraint, not proof of a deterministic callback: authors must avoid hidden state, floating intermediates, unstable ordering and external side effects. replay/deterministic supplies checked Q24.8 operations and integer queries; the duel uses fixed-width values, deterministic pool allocation and frame-owned RNG. Native arm64 and freestanding WASM execute the same four-seed 2,400-tick corpus to identical canonical state/event hashes.

Checksums are consistency diagnostics, not authentication or cheat resistance. The transport/roster provider must authenticate peers for deployments that need it. A peer can withhold inputs; the chosen policy stalls and ultimately disconnects after timeout. That does not establish fair-play adjudication.

Archives and participant recovery#

archive_capture, archive_encode, archive_decode and restore preserve the complete retained execution and protocol state. An archive contains its oldest retained frame and occurrences, subsequent input batches and per-tick digests, confirmed rolling hashes, speculative suffix, captured future local inputs, sparse received inputs, receive/ACK frontiers, roster and original match contract. Archives own their storage; destroy them with archive_destroy. The transport and callback/user pointers are supplied afresh and are never serialized.

Odin
archive: p2p.Archive(World, Input, Event, 2)
error = p2p.archive_capture(&peer, &archive)
bytes, error := p2p.archive_encode(&archive, model)
// Persist bytes with an application save boundary, then release owned storage.
// Decode into an empty Archive; restore into an empty, stable-address Runner.
report: p2p.Replay_Report
error = p2p.restore(&fresh_peer, &archive, model, roster, local_slot, fresh_transport,
                    report = &report)

The version-1 archive envelope is canonical, content/schema gated and limited to 16 MiB. Counts and exact payload length are checked before count-driven allocation. Restore validates frontiers and reexecutes the retained input sequence before installing the runtime. A changed model produces Replay_Mismatch with the first retained failing tick and expected/actual digest; failure releases staged storage. When the history ring wraps, the rolling hash retained at its oldest frame summarizes the discarded prefix. Restore verifies the retained suffix; it cannot reexecute frames no longer in the archive. Archives contain complete private world data, and CRC/hash checks provide integrity diagnostics, not authenticity.

Participants may restore together on fresh transport bindings, or one participant may restore while survivors retain their live runners and explicitly reconnect. Saves may have different receive/confirmation frontiers: protocol version 2 exchanges each peer's durable received frontier in Hello and resends any formerly acknowledged suffix it still retains. If a peer has received local inputs that this archive forgot, or the required retransmission history is gone, recovery fails with History. Old captured inputs are never regenerated. The admission provider must exclude old connection traffic and rebind the same ordered logical identities. transport.Remap supplies explicit, one-to-one logical to physical bindings; it does not authenticate them.

For a live rejoin, restore the returning participant's own archive, then call reconnect(&survivor, replacement_transport, monotonic_ms) on every affected survivor after the provider verifies the replacement bindings. This restarts Hello and its retry/timeout clock while retaining the survivor's exact timeline, captured inputs, ACK/receive frontiers, checksums and allocations. Advancement waits for the roster handshake. Reconnect is permitted after a timeout (Disconnected) or during a running/connecting session, at a settled runner boundary. It refuses failed/divergent runners, an active timeline operation, unresolved input repair, backward time and missing transport callbacks. Both transports are borrowed; the caller owns their lifetimes and retirement.

Odin
// Provider has authenticated the same ordered identities and fenced old traffic.
error = p2p.reconnect(&survivor, replacement_transport, monotonic_ms)
// Continue pumping and advancing normally once phase is Running.

The native Duel tests either participant returning. If the original listener returns, the surviving dialing process closes and reopens its ENet transport, rebuilds the logical mappings, and reconnects its retained runner. The remote physical server ID is again 1, but the connection is new. Closing the transport owner retires the old receive/delay buffers. This configured loopback provider is not authentication or source election; see the example's native creator-rejoin gate.

This requires a compatible durable archive. If a crashed player continued sampling after its last save, survivors may have inputs that the archive no longer contains; that recovery fails with History. A retained input log or another compatible save boundary is needed to cover that crash window. Reconnect does not choose another peer's world, change the roster, elect an authority or recover forgotten inputs. The caller must verify the replacement identity and exclude old traffic; reconnect does not perform those provider responsibilities.

Capture a settled Diverged runner to retain its mismatch metadata and local execution. Replaying with its original deterministic callback reproduces that execution and preserves the stopped phase. Replaying with a changed callback locates the first different retained state/event digest; it does not identify the root cause or prove that either participant was correct. Callback code is not serialized, so keep the corresponding build/content version with a recording. The Duel includes an offline verifier.

The two-process Godot recovery gate saves at speculative tick 240, kills both processes, binds fresh ENet IDs, restores and continues to tick 600 with reference world and occurrence reconciliation checks. Native-created session/divergence archives also decode and replay inside freestanding WASM to identical reports. The separate native rejoin_run.sh saves and kills only the dialing participant, keeps the listener alive through timeout, and restores against a new ENet binding. Both reach the same tick-600 world and reconciled occurrences. A three-player native/WASM corpus exercises two successive individual rejoins after timeout under four loss/jitter/duplication seeds, in default and speed builds. The browser Duel also exercises a single returning participant in fresh Chrome: its Save & pause control freezes capture before download, the process is killed, and its file is imported while the other browser retains the running match. The joining player receives a new physical RTC ID, rebound to its logical roster slot. The authenticated provider also supports the creator returning at the same ID 1 with a new connection generation. Delay/fragment/router buffers fence retired work; either survivor retains its runner. Both reach the tick-600 reference world.

Implemented behavior and remaining M7 work#

The initial runner, integer duel, loss/reordering/duplication tests, timeout, divergence checks and native two-process ENet gate exist. A lost input burst recovers through retransmission and bounded rollback. The Godot demo reconciles speculative events and compares the final world with an independent reference.

Confirmed spectators join a running match, replay received history, and reset explicitly after a blackout exceeds retained history. They use separate bounded transfer streams and never join the player confirmation roster. An admitted spectator can rebind to another participant using a retained state/event/chain anchor. The replacement must prove overlap; missing history or conflict is explicit. Native Duel and repeated native/WASM source-switch gates exercise this continuity contract. Optional profiling separates forward/replay/hash/pump wall time from capture-to-simulation input latency. Standalone benchmarks measure process CPU and the effect of fixed input-delay settings using matched recorded gameplay.

An initial authenticated admission provider checks fixed-roster credentials before initial binding and browser rejoin. It reuses the bounded challenged signaling frontend and supports full-mesh introductions.

Fixed-roster provisioning supplies durable room/invite enrollment, exact retries and authenticated incarnation changes. Its native TLS service/client and SQLite crash gates pass. The P2P party client connects browser Duel's invite menus to authenticated gameplay and fresh-process guest/creator return. The native P2P Direct owner supports authenticated two-player ENet and fresh-process endpoint replacement.

Roster changes, public authenticated provisioning, cross-native-platform execution and deployment integration remain pending. A copied Frame alone does not resume this session protocol. The fixed-point corpus and archive replay execute in WASM. The playable Duel also passes real WebRTC Chrome-process gates for delayed/lost inputs, a bounded blackout, late spectator reset and coordinated participant-file restoration. Public rendezvous/TURN and other browser engines are not established by these local gates. The archive retains a bounded diagnostic window, not a complete input/arrival log for arbitrarily long matches. Broader recording tools and field-level diffs remain debugger work.

See Replay Duel and the full roadmap. These tests cover the implemented fixed-roster behavior; remaining P2P capabilities and roadmap work need separate acceptance.
